method: Wash and dry the lettuce and tomato. Shred the lettuce and slice the tomato; put both on a clean plate, separate from the raw filling.
Split the wholemeal burger bun and toast the cut faces in a dry frying pan over a medium heat for 1–2 minutes. Set it on a clean plate.
Mix the measured light mayonnaise and tomato ketchup in a clean small bowl. Keep this finishing sauce separate from the uncooked filling and refrigerated until assembly.

Press the 5% beef mince into a patty about 1.5cm thick, slightly wider than the bun; no binder is needed. Coat with all the measured paprika and garlic powder. After handling raw 5% beef mince, wash hands and clean the board, knife and work surface before touching the ready-to-eat ingredients.

Heat the measured olive oil in the non-stick frying pan. Cook the beef patty over a medium heat for about 5–6 minutes on each side. Turn it carefully and leave it intact rather than repeatedly pressing it flat. Check the centre with a clean food thermometer: it must stay at 75°C or above for 30 seconds. Without a thermometer, cut the thickest piece open and check that it is steaming inside with no pink meat. Continue cooking until these checks are met; the suggested pan time alone is not a safety check.
Put the lettuce and tomato in the toasted bun, add the cooked beef patty and the cold finishing sauce, then close the bun and serve immediately.
